claim_a.text: On WMT 2014 English-to-German, the Transformer achieved a BLEU score more than 2 points above the previous best reported result.

claim_b.text: On the same WMT 2014 English-to-German evaluation and BLEU metric, the Transformer scored more than 2 points below the previous best reported result.

rationale: The claims use the same task, comparator and metric but assert opposite directions.

claim_a.text: The Transformer encoder and decoder dispense with recurrent layers and rely on attention and feed-forward layers.

claim_b.text: The same Transformer encoder and decoder require recurrent layers as their central sequence-processing component.

rationale: The claims make mutually exclusive statements about the same architecture.

claim_a.text: BERT pre-training conditions each token on both left and right context in all layers.

claim_b.text: Under the same BERT pre-training procedure, every token is conditioned only on left context in every layer.

rationale: Bidirectional and strictly left-context conditioning are incompatible under the stated same procedure.

claim_a.text: With the same retriever, generator and test split, increasing retrieved documents from 5 to 10 improved exact match.

claim_b.text: With the same retriever, generator and test split, increasing retrieved documents from 5 to 10 reduced exact match.

rationale: All stated conditions match and the direction of the result is opposite.

claim_a.text: On the same SQuAD 1.1 test set and exact-match metric, BERT-Large outperformed BERT-Base.

claim_b.text: On the same SQuAD 1.1 test set and exact-match metric, BERT-Base outperformed BERT-Large.

rationale: The same models are ranked in opposite orders under identical stated conditions.

claim_a.text: On WMT English-to-German, the Transformer improved BLEU and required less training time than the compared recurrent systems.

claim_b.text: On the same WMT English-to-German comparison, the Transformer improved BLEU but required more training time than the recurrent systems.

rationale: The BLEU conclusion agrees but the training-time conclusion conflicts.

claim_a.text: BERT-Large improved both GLUE aggregate score and SQuAD 1.1 exact match over BERT-Base.

claim_b.text: Under the same evaluations, BERT-Large improved GLUE aggregate score but reduced SQuAD 1.1 exact match relative to BERT-Base.

rationale: The GLUE statement agrees while the SQuAD statement conflicts.

claim_a.text: RAG improved factuality and reduced parameter-only knowledge dependence on the evaluated generation task.

claim_b.text: On the same task, RAG improved factuality but increased dependence on parameter-only knowledge.

rationale: One material conclusion agrees and the other is reversed.

claim_a.text: The Transformer reached 28.4 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-German.

claim_b.text: The Transformer reached 41.8 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-French.

rationale: The language pair differs, so different BLEU values are not contradictory.

claim_a.text: BERT-Large obtained a higher F1 score on SQuAD 1.1 than BERT-Base.

claim_b.text: BERT-Base obtained a higher accuracy score on SWAG than a separately trained BERT-Large run.

rationale: The dataset, metric and run differ.

claim_a.text: RAG-Sequence improved exact match on Natural Questions using a Wikipedia index.

claim_b.text: A closed-book generator improved ROUGE-L on CNN/DailyMail without a retrieval index.

rationale: The method, dataset and metric differ, so the outcomes are not competing answers to one proposition.

claim_a.text: Full self-attention has O(n squared times d) per-layer complexity.

claim_b.text: Restricted self-attention with neighborhood size r has O(r times n times d) per-layer complexity.

rationale: The statements concern explicitly different attention variants.

claim_a.text: With 100 percent of the training data, BERT achieved the reported task score.

claim_b.text: With 10 percent of the training data, BERT achieved a lower score on the same task.

rationale: The explicitly different sample sizes can explain the score difference.

claim_a.text: The Transformer removes recurrence from its sequence transduction architecture.

claim_b.text: The proposed Transformer performs sequence transduction without recurrent layers.

rationale: The claims are paraphrases of the same architectural property.

claim_a.text: BERT uses masked language modeling during pre-training.

claim_b.text: During pre-training, BERT predicts selected masked input tokens.

rationale: Both describe the masked-language-model objective.

claim_a.text: RAG combines parametric generation with retrieved non-parametric memory.

claim_b.text: The RAG model conditions a generator on documents fetched from an external index.

rationale: The claims give compatible descriptions of retrieval-augmented generation.

claim_a.text: The Transformer uses multi-head self-attention to build contextual representations.

claim_b.text: BERT builds contextual representations using a multi-layer bidirectional Transformer encoder.

rationale: The claims are compatible at the shared proposition that Transformer attention builds contextual representations.

claim_a.text: The Transformer decoder masks future positions during autoregressive training.

claim_b.text: RAG retrieves passages from a Wikipedia index for open-domain question answering.

rationale: The claims address different system components and propositions.

claim_a.text: BERT fine-tunes a classification output layer for GLUE tasks.

claim_b.text: Sinusoidal positional encodings represent token positions in the Transformer.

rationale: Fine-tuning a classifier and positional encoding do not answer the same proposition.

claim_a.text: The RAG document index uses a fixed Wikipedia snapshot.

claim_b.text: BERT uses WordPiece tokenization with a fixed vocabulary.

rationale: The knowledge corpus and tokenizer vocabulary are different objects.

claim_a.text: Eight GPUs were used for the reported English-to-French training run.

claim_b.text: Next sentence prediction is one of BERT's pre-training objectives.

rationale: Hardware count and a pre-training objective are unrelated propositions.

claim_a.text: The model performed better in the reported experiment.

claim_b.text: The other model performed worse in its experiment.

rationale: The models, experiments, datasets, metrics and comparison direction are unspecified.

claim_a.text: Pre-training helped on some downstream tasks.

claim_b.text: Pre-training did not help in another evaluation.

rationale: The downstream tasks and evaluation conditions are absent, so comparability cannot be established.

claim_a.text: Retrieval changed the output quality.

claim_b.text: Retrieval did not change the relevant outcome.

rationale: Neither output quality nor relevant outcome is defined, so a direct contradiction is not supportable.
